title: INT4 runtime conversion bug causing intermittent inference failures and probability skew
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a limited rollout of the new INT4 conversion pipeline (auto-conversion + per-layer scaling), we observed an uptick in inference failures and degraded output quality across a subset of models. Symptoms included intermittent 502/5xx responses, crash loops in the serving container for some model variants, and measurable shift in token-probability distributions (KL divergence) compared to FP16 baselines.

Impact:
- Customer-facing endpoints using the new INT4 variant saw increased error rates for ~3 hours (partial mitigation in place).
- Automated eval harness showed median token-level KL divergence increase from 0.01 to 0.12 on the affected set, and a 6% rise in top-1 edit-distance for generation tests.
- A small percentage of requests returned nonsensical tokens (probability skew) leading to downstream application errors.

Detection / timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-09 23:48: Canary probe alerted on increased soft-fail rate for the INT4 variant.
- 2026-03-10 00:05: Pager duty triggered after 3x spike in 5xx for INT4 route.
- 2026-03-10 00:12: Emergency routing to FP16 variant enabled for affected customer segments.
- 2026-03-10 01:00: Rolling pause of INT4 rollout; ops team implemented strict throttling.

Initial root cause hypothesis and confirmation:
- Root cause: an off-by-one in the INT4 scaling quantizer for weight tensors of fused attention kernels when layer normalization epsilon was below a threshold. This produced incorrect symmetric scale factors that could overflow during accumulation for certain activations, leading to two observable problems: (1) a skewed softmax distribution (probability mass collapse) and (2) memory layout mismatch triggering a runtime assertion in the fused attention path on older CUDA kernels, which caused crash loops for the serving process.
- Confirmation: reproducer notebooks added to the repo produce the same KL divergence and assertion failures when the epsilon condition is met and the converter uses the new symmetric-scaling code path.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Immediate: traffic routing rule applied to send >95% of production traffic to FP16 variants and reserve INT4 for internal canaries only. (Owner: SRE, Marco Li)
- Hotfix: reverted the new symmetric-scaling code path in the conversion pipeline and re-enabled legacy scaling for affected architectures. Hotfix PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4721 (Owner: Engine-Quant team, Priya Menon).
- Monitoring: added emergency Grafana panel showing per-layer activation ranges and token-level KL divergence for each canary model.

Longer-term corrective actions (action items):
1) Conversion pipeline hardening (Owner: Priya Menon) — Due 2026-03-21
   - Add unit/integration tests that exercise low-epsilon LN and fused-kernel weight layouts across representative models.
   - Add scalar range checks and guard rails during conversion; abort & fall back to legacy quantization when guard trips.
   - Publish a conversion compatibility matrix indicating which fused kernels are safe for symmetric vs asymmetric scaling.

2) Operator compatibility & CI (Owner: Daniel Park) — Due 2026-04-04
   - Extend CI matrix to include older CUDA/cuDNN versions that surfaced the crash loop.
   - Add nightly stress runs that execute fused attention kernels under INT4 on multiple driver/kernel combinations.
   - Fail builds early on layout/stride mismatches.

3) Canary & metric improvements (Owner: Marco Li) — Due 2026-03-18
   - Add KL-divergence and softmax-temperature drift metrics to canary dashboards and define SLOs/alerts.
   - Add per-layer activation histogram drift alerts and a signal that triggers automatic rollback of a variant.

4) Rollout & rollback automation (Owner: SRE lead, Emma Johnson) — Due 2026-03-25
   - Implement automated rollback of model variants when token-level quality or error-rate thresholds exceed limits for >5 minutes.
   - Integrate rollback with rollout policy to allow canary-only enablement for new quantization converters.

5) Customer and partner communication (Owner: Customer Success, Ben Ramos) — Due 2026-03-15
   - Notify impacted customers with incident summary and mitigation steps.
   - Offer assistance to re-route to FP16 or dedicated capacity while INT4 stabilizes.

6) Post-incident docs and runbook updates (Owner: Aisha Patel) — Due 2026-03-17
   - Update the quantization rollout runbook with new preflight checks and a checklist for enabling INT4 in production.
   - Document the compatibility matrix and known unsafe configurations.

Open questions / trade-offs discussed:
- Symmetric vs asymmetric scaling: symmetric scaling simplifies integer math but is riskier on fused kernels with atypical layernorm params. We decided to maintain symmetric scaling as an opt-in path for models that explicitly pass the preflight checks; default will remain conservative (legacy asymmetric) until more validation is complete.
- Canary sensitivity: tighter thresholds reduce rollout velocity but significantly limit customer exposure. Team agreed to narrow windows for initial rollouts and progressively relax as signals stabilize.

Acceptance criteria for "Done":
- New unit + integration tests merged and green for converter paths.
- Canary dashboards emit clear alerts and rollback automation implemented in staging.
- Compatibility matrix published and conversion pipeline fails fast on unsupported layouts.
- Customer outreach completed for all impacted accounts.

Notes and follow-ups:
- Related issues created for implementation subtasks: ENG-12012 (converter tests), ENG-12013 (CI matrix expansion), ENG-12014 (rollback automation).
- Keep INT4 route disabled for broad production rollout until all actions complete and we have two weeks of stable canary metrics.
